niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
Great question — “shadow work” and “spiritual practice” overlap a lot but can come from very different traditions and methods (Jungian psychology, somatic/trauma‑informed work, Buddhist/meditation traditions, nondual spirituality, breathwork/energy work, etc.). Below are reputable online options organized by approach, with who each is best for and safety notes to help you choose.

Top recommended platforms & courses (by approach)

- Jungian / shadow-focused
  - Jung Platform — ongoing short courses and multi‑week programs taught by Jungian analysts (James Hollis, Donald Kalsched, others). Best for structured Jungian shadow/archetype study and practical exercises. Format: recorded lessons + Q&A/workshops. Price: per course or subscription.
  - Sounds True (Debbie Ford materials and related programs) — has classic shadow integration content and related teacher programs. Good introduction to shadow concepts and guided practices. (Note: Debbie Ford’s work is an entry point; combine with trauma‑informed approaches if needed.)

- Trauma‑informed / somatic integration
  - iRest (Integrative Restoration) Foundation — trauma‑sensitive meditation practice with online trainings and short courses. Great for people who need a gentle, embodied approach to inner work.
  - Somatic Experiencing / Sensorimotor Psychotherapy — professional trainings are long and intensive, but both organizations offer public workshops/intro courses. Best if you have trauma history or want body‑based safety/grounding skills before deeper shadow work.

- Mindfulness & meditation foundations (highly recommended before deep shadow work)
  - Palouse Mindfulness — a well-regarded free, self‑paced MBSR (Mindfulness‑Based Stress Reduction) course. Excellent foundation for emotional regulation and present‑moment skills.
  - Waking Up app (Sam Harris) or apps like Headspace/Calm — structured secular meditation courses to build daily practice and attention.
  - University/ MOOC courses (Coursera/FutureLearn) — search for MBSR, “Mindfulness and Well‑Being,” or “The Science of Well‑Being” (Yale) for psychological groundwork.

- Spiritual / nondual teachers & retreats
  - Eckhart Tolle School of Awakening, Rupert Spira, Adyashanti — each offers paid online courses and recorded satsangs/retreats that focus on presence, inquiry, and nondual realization. Good if your priority is spiritual awakening alongside inner work.
  - Sounds True & Gaia — host many spiritual teachers and multi‑week online retreats; format and depth vary.

- Mixed/transformational platforms
  - Mindvalley — high‑production transformational programs (energy work, inner child, personal transformation). Good for community support and structured courses; more commercial.
  - Insight Timer — huge free library of guided meditations and a marketplace of paid mini‑courses. Useful for sampling many teachers cheaply.

- Practical/self‑help style courses
  - Udemy / Skillshare — many practical “shadow work” and inner‑child courses. Quality varies—check reviews and instructor credentials. Good if you want inexpensive, practical exercises.

How to pick the right course
- Clarify your goal: theraputic healing (trauma? severe symptoms?), emotional self‑work (inner child, patterns), or spiritual awakening. Different courses fit different aims.
- If you have a trauma history or current mental‑health concerns: prioritize trauma‑informed or somatic programs (iRest, somatic psych, or a therapist‑led course).
- Start with a foundation in mindfulness/grounding before doing intense shadow work.
- Read reviews, check instructor credentials (clinical or long-term practice experience), and look for courses that include integration/practical tools, not just heavy theory.

Safety & ethical notes
- Shadow work can bring up strong emotions, memories, dissociation, or panic. If you have active PTSD, suicidal thoughts, or unstable mental health, do this work with a licensed therapist or clinician.
- Start slowly: short meditations, journaling prompts, grounding exercises, and an integration plan (rest, community/support).
- Have a safety plan: therapist contact, crisis resources, and self‑soothing tools (breath, grounding, somatic movements).

Suggested learning pathway (gentle)
1. Build basic stability: 4–8 weeks of mindfulness (Palouse MBSR or a daily meditation course).
2. Intro to shadow concepts: a Jungian intro (Jung Platform or a short Sounds True course) and reading: Meeting the Shadow / The Dark Side of the Light Chasers.
3. Somatic & integration work: iRest or somatic workshops to learn grounding and resourcing.
4. Deeper programs/retreats: longer shadow integration programs, guided group work, or a trusted teacher/retreat for sustained work.

Short reading/listening starters
- Books: Meeting the Shadow (Zweig & Abrams), The Dark Side of the Light Chasers (Debbie Ford), Owning Your Own Shadow (Robert A. Johnson)
- Teachers/apps: Tara Brach, Jack Kornfield, Sam Harris (Waking Up), Insight Timer for free guided practices

If you want, I can:
- Recommend 3–5 specific courses matched to your goals (therapeutic healing vs. spiritual awakening vs. self‑exploration). 
- Give a week‑by‑week starter plan (meditation + journaling + shadow prompts) you can follow safely.

Which direction are you leaning — more therapeutic (healing trauma/patterns) or more spiritual (awakening/presence)?
